text.text: The Amstrad GX4000 was released in 1990 as a cartridge-based video game console derived from the Amstrad CPC Plus computer line. It was Amstrad's attempt to enter the home console market during the fourth generation of gaming hardware. The system featured improved graphics compared with earlier CPC computers and used cartridge software instead of cassette or disk media. Its library included games such as Burnin' Rubber, Switchblade, Robocop 2, and Batman: The Movie. The GX4000 competed against established systems including the Nintendo Entertainment System, Sega Master System, and TurboGrafx-16. Limited software support and the rapid growth of 16-bit consoles contributed to its short lifespan. The GX4000 was discontinued after roughly one year, making it one of the shortest-lived console platforms based on an existing computer architecture.
